pr.title: Encrypt backups under a passphrase (1.2c)
pr.body:
Phase 1.2c: passphrase-protected backups.

## The problem
A backup holds every secret of the installation: route and external account passwords, the relay password and the SRS secret. Secret settings went into the archive in plain text. Account and route passwords were encrypted under a key that every copy of the server shared. Anyone who could read the backup file could read the secrets.

## What changes
- **Backups with a passphrase** (at least 12 characters, the same minimum as for exporting the secret key):
  - 7-Zip encrypts the whole archive with AES-256, file names included (`-mhe=on`).
  - Messages go into the archive instead of next to it.
  - The secrets inside are plain, so the backup restores on any computer, given the passphrase.
  - Without the passphrase, 7-Zip can't open the archive. The server won't open it with a wrong passphrase or none.
- **Backups without a passphrase:** secrets stay protected under the installation's key, as in the database. They restore on the same installation, or on another one once the key is imported.
- **Backups from earlier versions:** `BackupInformation` now records which of the two applies. A backup from an earlier version records neither, and restores as before.
- **Logs:** the passphrase is masked (`-p***`) in every logged 7za command line.
- **COM:**
  - `BackupSettings.Passphrase` (write-only; empty removes it).
  - `BackupSettings.PassphraseIsSet`.
  - `BackupManager.LoadEncryptedBackup(file, passphrase)`, which fails with "Check the passphrase…" when the archive can't be read.
- **Administrator:**
  - Backup tab: an "Encrypt with a passphrase" option with passphrase and confirm fields.
  - Restore tab: a passphrase field and an Open button.
- **Schema 5714:** a `backuppassphrase` setting, stored as a secret. Includes upgrade scripts for all four databases, the `CreateTables` scripts, `REQUIRED_DB_VERSION` and DBUpdater.

## Tests
`Infrastructure/BackupPassphrase.cs`:
- A short passphrase is refused; `PassphraseIsSet` follows the setting.
- An encrypted backup restores with its passphrase, and the route password still authenticates.
- An encrypted backup doesn't open without the passphrase: `7za t` fails with a wrong one, `LoadBackup` finds nothing in it, and `LoadEncryptedBackup` with a wrong passphrase throws.
- A backup without a passphrase has no plain secrets in its XML (`Secrets="InstallationKey"`, `aes1:` values), and restores the route password.
- A backup in the earlier format (Blowfish route password, no `Secrets` attribute) still restores the route password.

+// Copyright (c) 2010 Martin Knafve / hMailServer.com.
+// http://www.hmailserver.com
+
+#pragma once
+
+namespace HM
+{
+   // How the secrets in a backup - the passwords of external accounts and routes, the relay
+   // password, the SRS secret and the backup passphrase - are written into its XML and read
+   // back, set by BackupExecuter for the backup or restore it runs. One runs at a time.
+   class BackupSecrets
+   {
+   public:
+
+      enum Mode
+      {
+         // A backup with a passphrase: the whole archive is encrypted under it, so the secrets
+         // inside are plain, and the backup restores on any computer that has the passphrase.
+         ProtectedByArchive,
+
+         // A backup without one: the secrets are protected under the installation's secret key,
+         // as in the database. Restoring them on another computer needs that key imported.
+         ProtectedByInstallationKey,
+
+         // A backup made by an earlier version, which says neither: passwords of accounts and
+         // routes Blowfish-encrypted (or under the installation's key), settings plain.
+         Legacy
+      };
+
+      static void SetMode(Mode mode);
+
+      // The value to write into the XML for a secret.
+      static String Store(const String &plain);
+
+      // The secret a value read from the XML stands for. A setting was written plain by earlier
+      // versions; the passwords of accounts and routes were encrypted.
+      static String LoadPassword(const String &stored);
+      static String LoadSetting(const String &stored);
+
+      // The BackupInformation attribute that says how a backup holds its secrets.
+      static String ModeName(Mode mode);
+      static Mode ModeFromName(const String &name);
+
+   private:
+
+      static Mode mode_;
+   };
+}

commit.message:
Encrypt backups under a passphrase

A backup holds every secret of the installation: route and external
account passwords, the relay password, the SRS secret. Settings were
written plain into the archive, and the rest under a key every copy
of the server shared.

Backups can now be encrypted under a passphrase of at least 12
characters. 7-Zip encrypts the whole archive with AES-256, file names
included (-mhe=on), and the messages go into the archive instead of
next to it. The secrets inside are plain, so the backup restores on
any computer, given the passphrase. The passphrase is masked in the
logged 7za command lines.

A backup without a passphrase now keeps its secrets protected under the
installation's key, as in the database. BackupInformation records which
of the two applies. A backup made by an earlier version records
neither, and restores as before.

COM: BackupSettings.Passphrase (write-only), BackupSettings.PassphraseIsSet
and BackupManager.LoadEncryptedBackup. Administrator: an "Encrypt with a
passphrase" option on the Backup tab, and a passphrase field on the
Restore tab. The passphrase is stored as a secret setting, under schema
version 5714.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Fix database creation and backup COM error messages

The scripts that create the database are split into statements at blank
lines. The backuppassphrase insert had none before it, so it ran together
with the one above: MySQL rejected the script, and the internal database
was not created.

BackupSettings and BackupManager did not implement ISupportErrorInfo, so
the messages of the errors they return - a passphrase that is too short,
a backup the passphrase does not open - reached callers as a bare HRESULT.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
